Compare a lifter with similar competition performances

Source: R/compare_lifter.R
compare_lifter.Rd

Filters historical competition results by sex, equipment and a bodyweight window, optionally adding an age window. It then calculates empirical percentiles for squat, bench press, deadlift and total. A percentile is the percentage of matching performances less than or equal to the entered lift.

Usage

compare_lifter(
  data = NULL,
  sex,
  equipment,
  bodyweight,
  squat,
  bench,
  deadlift,
  age = NULL,
  bodyweight_tolerance = 5,
  age_tolerance = 5,
  min_n = 30
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the same fields as powerlifting, or NULL to use the packaged data.

sex

One of "F" or "M".

equipment

One of "Raw", "Wraps", "Single-ply", or "Multi-ply".

bodyweight

Bodyweight in kilograms.

squat, bench, deadlift

Best successful lifts in kilograms.

age

Optional age in years. If NULL, age is not used for matching.

bodyweight_tolerance

Maximum difference in bodyweight, in kilograms, for a performance to be considered similar.

age_tolerance

Maximum age difference in years when age is supplied.

min_n

Minimum desired peer-group size. The result is still returned below this threshold, with weak_sample set to TRUE.

Value

A list containing summary, a four-row data frame of lift values and percentiles; peers, the filtered records; n, the peer count; weak_sample; weakest_lift; and the applied filters.

Examples

result <- compare_lifter(
  powerlifting, sex = "F", equipment = "Raw", bodyweight = 63,
  squat = 110, bench = 60, deadlift = 140
)
result$summary
#>                 lift entered_kg peer_median_kg percentile
#> squat_kg       Squat        110          102.5       64.7
#> bench_kg       Bench         60           57.5       59.2
#> deadlift_kg Deadlift        140          127.5       70.1
#> total_kg       Total        310          290.0       65.0
result$weakest_lift
#> [1] "Bench"
